findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In 'Design of the fix', add a short prior-art comparison justifying the hand-rolled interprocedural owner resolver over (a) using mypy — already installed and run as `make typecheck` on this tree — to resolve attribute reads to their owning dataclass, and (b) vulture's whitelist model for the dynamic-read false-positive class; state concretely why each established approach is unsuitable (anti-repackaging / Rule-of-Three).
evidence: Plan: 'resolve the RECEIVER expression of each ast.Attribute read to a set of candidate owning schema classes ... and a cross-module fixed point that binds unannotated PARAMETERS from their call sites' — this is interprocedural type inference done by hand.

The final AC already runs `make typecheck`, confirming mypy is part of the toolchain; `resolve_symbol('mypy')` => EXISTS in the installed environment. mypy natively resolves an attribute read to its owning class, which is the exact resolution problem the plan re-implements.

duckduckgo_search: vulture (github.com/jendrikseipp/vulture) is a mature AST dead-code detector with a whitelist model for exactly the dynamic/implicit-read false positives the plan calls 'required negative fixtures'; the plan does not mention it.

ABSENCE: the plan's 'Design of the fix' and 'Failure direction' subsections argue correctness empirically but contain no comparison to any existing type checker or dead-code tool and no justification for building the resolver in-house.
findings.finding: The plan commits to a hand-rolled interprocedural attribute-owner resolver (cross-module fixed-point parameter binding, return-annotation binding, assignment propagation, IfExp/BoolOp handling) without considering the established prior art that already resolves attribute reads to their owning dataclass: mypy (installed in this environment and already run as `make typecheck` on this very tree, e.g. via a plugin or a targeted query) and vulture (a well-known AST-based dead-code detector whose whitelist mechanism directly parallels the plan's `# read-via:` markers / negative fixtures). Reinventing a slice of type inference in a CI script needs an anti-repackaging / Rule-of-Three justification against these; the 'Design of the fix' section supplies none.
findings.location: Section 'Design of the fix', step 2 (per-read owner resolution / cross-module fixed point)
scenarios: A future field is read through a receiver shape the hand-rolled resolver does not model (e.g. dict-of-configs, comprehension binding, decorator-wrapped accessor) — mypy would resolve it, the bespoke resolver false-flags it and breaks CI.
Maintenance burden: the interprocedural fixed point must be re-verified whenever config plumbing changes, whereas a mypy-backed approach tracks the language.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Prior art' paragraph: note that mypy already type-checks this tree and can resolve attribute owners (e.g. via a plugin or `reveal_type`/API query), and that vulture solves dead-attribute detection with whitelists; then justify the bespoke resolver only if those are genuinely inadequate (e.g. cost of a mypy plugin, inability to key on schema sections) — otherwise adopt the existing tool.
